text:
B: Hello, can you hear me?
A: Yes, hello. I hear you good. I am Tomasz.
B: Abdirahman. I'm in Leicester.
A: Warrington. So you are East Midlands. What do you do, Abdirahman?
B: Vehicle technician. Vans, mostly, at a fleet depot. Servicing, diagnostics, repairs.
A: Ah, then I must ask you something. My brother has a small building firm, and his van broke down again last week. Second time this year. The garage said it is the, er, the EGR valve. Is that a real thing or they are just taking his money?
B: No, that's real, yeah. Very common on the diesels. If he's doing short runs, site to site, it clogs up. They don't get hot enough to burn it off, you know. What van is it?
A: Transit. Quite old.
B: Yeah, that'll be it. Tell him to give it a proper run on the motorway now and then. Half an hour, decent speed. Helps a lot.
A: Okay, I will tell him. He will say it is my fault anyway.
B: Ha. Brothers, yeah.
A: Exactly. I live with him, so I hear about this van every day.
B: What do you do yourself?
A: I am student, civil engineering, second year at Salford. Before, I was eleven years supervisor in a warehouse. Then I decided, okay, I am forty-something, if I want to do this, I must do it now. So I did the Access course in the evenings, and now university full-time. It is hard, some modules, but I like the practical ones. Structures, materials. Not so much the theory.
B: That's a big change, fair play.
A: Some days I feel very old in the lecture. But the young ones come to ask me for help with the calculations, so maybe I am useful.
B: Yeah, I get that a bit with the apprentices. They just come and stand there till you show them.
A: You train them?
B: Yeah, I'm senior on my shift now. Sign off their jobs, show them stuff. They're alright mostly. One of them tried to put the wrong oil in a van last week, so.
A: Oh no. You caught it?
B: Yeah, before he started it, luckily.
A: Good. In the warehouse, the young ones, same. You must check everything twice.
B: Yeah. Paperwork's my problem, though. My supervisor's always chasing my job sheets.
A: Ha. I am opposite. I have spreadsheet for everything. My marks, my timetable.
B: You'd get on with my supervisor, then.
A: Probably. You play football? I saw a hi-vis in your photo, I thought, he is like me, just home from work.
B: Yeah, it was after a shift. Five-a-side on Wednesdays. Gets rained off half the time.
A: Same in Warrington. Everything rains off. Who do you support, Leicester?
B: Yeah, Leicester City. You?
A: Legia Warszawa, from Poland. And a little bit Warrington Wolves, rugby league. My son likes them more than...
